title: Four Swedish lake samples gave no clear warmth and colour interaction in Gonyostomum share in 1995-2022
abstract: We tested whether warm June-July weather had a stronger link to August Gonyostomum semen share in browner lake-years. We joined public lake records to GHCN-CAMS air temperature. Four North and South samples in 1995-2008 and 2009-2022 contained 2,766 lake-years at 110 lakes. Models controlled lake and year effects, total phosphorus, total organic carbon and pH. The warmth by within-lake log-colour estimates were -1.13, -1.44, -0.25 and -0.003 percentage points per C per colour doubling. All four adjusted intervals included zero. Lake trends, genus aggregation, occurrence and first differences gave no repeated positive result. Current-minus-future interaction intervals also included zero. In the later southern sample, two-way cluster subtraction gave a much smaller standard error than either one-way method. Two sensitivity fits gave negative variance estimates and no valid interval. We show wider uncertainty checks and do not infer absence of an interaction. Sparse northern records, 14 years per fit, annual chemical values, coarse weather and unmeasured sampling changes limit inference. Relative share does not measure absolute bloom biomass. The package gives code, a derived panel, all results, source hashes, a figure and a separate numerical check. It tests no direct air pollution effect.

display.caption: Warmth by colour estimates for four Swedish lake samples. Both panels use the largest of the two-way and two one-way cluster standard errors, with four-test critical values. This is a wider uncertainty check, not proof of nominal coverage. Zero lies in all shown intervals. Share is relative biovolume.

citations.reason: The prior campaign study found recording effects in littoral invertebrate richness. We test a new phytoplankton outcome from the same monitoring programme; no code or numeric result was reused.
CC0 Swedish lake data, version 1, physicochemical and Hellinger phytoplankton tables.
The 2025 source study gives the sampling method and broad climate-composition results. This work tests a specified within-lake interaction, not its full multivariate result.
Temperature and other factors were proposed as drivers of Gonyostomum expansion. It motivates the interaction question; data may overlap this national programme.
Iron, pH and nutrients complicate the interpretation of water colour. Our table has no iron measurements; national monitoring records can overlap.
Prior northern-lake study found different chemical associations by phytoplankton group. Its records can overlap ours.
